column1: # How a request's body value is written into its row, and how any JSON value a row holds is written (the canonical
# form): one table for the course (Source/, Python: w2cplatform/canonical.py, SpecConsole._file_request) and the
# product (Go: canonjson.go, requests.go). THIS IS THE COURSE'S SEED: the shared table is «Паритет»'s
# (testdata/requests_body.tsv in the product), and when its committed main keeps one, this file is a copy of it, byte
# Each row is filed as `POST /requests {"unit": <a unit>, "v": <raw>}` in a family whose schema says of `v` only
# `maxLength: 32`, and the row's field `v` is read back.
# Columns, tab-separated, one row a line; a line that begins with '#' and an empty line are no row:
#   raw      the value as the body carries it, JSON text exactly as sent (`5.0` is not `5`)
#   written  the text of the row's field: a string as it is, without quotes; true/false; a number whose value is whole
#            in integer digits — an integer in exactly the digits it came with, never through a float — any other in
#            its shortest decimal form, never an exponent; a list or a map as canonical JSON (compact, keys sorted,
#            UTF-8 as it is: control characters as JSON writes them, \b \f \n \r \t short, U+2028/U+2029 raw, < > & /
#            not escaped). Two words are no text: (absent) — the row has no such field (`null`); (refused) — the request
#            is refused, 400 (not JSON; or the text is longer than the schema's maxLength, a number's text too)
#   note     why the row is here
# A text that would hold a tab or a line break is no row here: the table could not say it.
